summary: Board extract for the One Group, Many Practices integration programme, June 2024. Covers the programme launch, workstream owners and status, the Durnesswick integration and its brand and LIMS steps, the open price harmonisation and archive decisions, and the risks the board asked to see. Final version for the June board, with minor wording changes from the draft circulated to workstream owners.

properties.subject: Integration programme board update

slides.title: Integration board update
slides.subtitle:
One Group, Many Practices
Q2 2024 board meeting
Sofia Lindervik, Integration Director

slides.title: Purpose of this update
bullets: Report progress on the integration programme since the board approved its scope in April
Confirm the workstream owners and their current status
Bring forward the Durnesswick integration decisions for approval
Set out the decisions on price and archive that we still need from the board

slides.title: Programme principle
bullets: One Group, Many Practices: local scientific operations are retained while shared processes converge
Shared functions move to group ownership first: HR, finance, IT and commercial reporting
Local client relationships, study direction and accession numbering are not changed without a specific decision
Each firm's legacy records are kept as they are unless a retention or access decision says otherwise
slides.notes: This principle is the test for every workstream decision. Two items on today's agenda are exceptions and are flagged as such.

rows: Started; local currencies and discounts under review
Common master agreed; migration planned by firm
Directory consolidation under way for early firms
Local shares to be preserved as archive roots

slides.title: Durnesswick Laboratories: integration status
bullets: Durnesswick joined the group on 1 February 2024 and is the first firm to join under the programme
Formulation and early CMC work continues with its own scientific leadership and client contracts
Brand migration to the common master is the next visible step, and is planned for the second half of the year
Durnesswick's LIMS cutover is not yet scheduled and will follow the export dictionary decision

slides.title: Brand migration
bullets: Common master template and brand guide agreed with the group communications lead
Firms A to E are sequenced for migration, starting with client-facing templates
Legacy records will not be restyled; only documents issued from migration onwards use the master
Durnesswick will migrate its templates first, followed by its signature blocks and report headers

slides.title: LIMS consolidation
bullets: Draft export dictionary covers the fields that group reporting needs from each firm
Local accession numbers will be kept for all firms, which the board is asked to confirm
Cutover dates are not set; the draft plan will come back to the board after firm-level reviews
Quality review of the export fields is under way with each site head

slides.title: Price harmonisation: current position
bullets: Price lists and service names are being gathered firm by firm, starting with the older acquisitions
Historical currencies and discounts are recorded as they stand and not netted off
No group price rule has been proposed yet, and no quote should be assumed to follow one
A decision on the normalisation approach is needed from the board before the mapping can be finished

slides.title: Cross-sell and client identity
bullets: A client identity bridge is being built so that one customer is not treated as two by different firms
Subsidiary and lookalike name checks are required before any cross-sell approach is made
No cross-sell activity should start with a client until its identity has been checked against the bridge
Commercial leads have agreed to hold back joint approaches until the first bridge review

slides.title: HR and payroll
bullets: Directory consolidation is under way and will reach firms A to F in turn
Payroll stays with each firm until its directory entries are confirmed
Staff at Durnesswick are on the group directory from the start of integration
The group will not onboard a firm's payroll until its leavers and contractors are reconciled

slides.title: IT and archive migration
bullets: Local shares are being kept as archive roots rather than merged into the group estate
Leaver folders need an owner's sign-off before they move or are deleted
Retention decisions are not yet made for the older shares and are listed as open
No shared drive content will be deleted as part of the migration without written approval
slides.notes: The board asked last quarter what happens to leaver folders. This is the current answer, and it will be checked again at the next update.

slides.title: Risks
bullets: Price mapping could lock in historical discounts that clients expect to keep, which the commercial team is watching closely
Brand migration may leave mixed templates in client hands if the legacy records are not clearly marked
LIMS cutover dates depend on firm-level reviews that have not yet been scheduled
Archive decisions could slip if ownership of leaver folders is not confirmed in time

slides.title: Decisions requested from the board
bullets: Approve the Durnesswick integration plan for brand, LIMS and HR steps
Confirm that local accession numbers are retained for all firms
Agree that the price normalisation approach comes back to the board in the autumn
Note the archive hold for legacy shares until ownership checks are complete

slides.title: Next steps
bullets: Workstream owners to return updated plans by the end of June 2024
Durnesswick brand migration plan to be circulated to the firm's leadership team
Client identity bridge review at the next steering meeting
Next board update in the autumn with the price approach and LIMS plan
